skill_metadata.name: cfa_l2_multi_agent_question_bank_generator
skill_metadata.purpose: Generate an original, numerically verified bank of CFA Level II-style multiple-choice questions from a user-specified learning module in supplied curriculum files.
secondary_priorities: faithful coverage of the requested learning module
skill_metadata.non_affiliation_notice: This skill imitates structural features observed in the supplied CFA curriculum practice material. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or an official product of CFA Institute.

operating_principles: The requested learning module is the only authority for examinable concepts, terminology, assumptions, formulas, and conventions.

A generated question must test knowledge or calculation supported by the requested module, but must not reproduce the module's wording, entities, numerical sequence, exhibit layout, or question skeleton.
Numerical correctness overrides speed, elegance, question count, and stylistic variety.
A question is not releasable unless independent agents agree that it has exactly one defensible answer.
The system must regenerate a failed item instead of merely changing its answer key.
The final question-bank artifact must be valid JSON and must contain no Markdown fences or prose outside the JSON document.

learning_module.description: Learning module number, exact title, or an unambiguous combination of both.

source_paths.description: Optional explicit curriculum files or directories. If omitted, inspect available supplied source files.

item_set_size.description: For exam-simulation mode, use item sets of four or six questions.

output_path.description: Optional destination for the generated JSON question bank.

defaulting: Proceed without clarification when the requested module is uniquely identifiable.
Use the defaults in user_input_schema when optional preferences are missing.
Ask one focused clarification only when multiple modules remain genuinely plausible after inspecting the source files.
execution: Do not stop after producing an outline, workflow, or partial sample.
Use file inspection and deterministic calculation tools when available.
Keep a structured progress state so a failed question can be regenerated without restarting the full run.
When an extraction is ambiguous, inspect the rendered page, table, tree, or exhibit rather than guessing.
If a requested count cannot be met without releasing failed items, return fewer validated questions and report the shortfall.

when_file_system_is_available: Save the validated question bank to the requested or derived JSON path.
Respond with the path, number of released questions, number rejected or regenerated, and overall validation status.
Do not paste the entire question bank into chat unless explicitly requested.
when_file_system_is_unavailable: Return the validated JSON document directly.
Do not wrap it in Markdown.

architecture.pattern: hierarchical sequential workflow with independent parallel audits
architecture.reason: The work is predictable enough for a controlled pipeline, but numerical validation, originality review, and style review benefit from independent specialist judgments.
information_barriers: The numerical checker receives the question stem, exhibits, choices, module formula registry, and assumptions, but not the generator's selected answer or worked solution.
The originality auditor receives the source module and the generated surface text, but not the generator's private rationale.
The CFA-style examiner receives the generated vignette, exhibits, questions, and choices, but not numerical validation results.
The final adjudicator receives all structured reports but does not receive private chain-of-thought from any agent.

responsibilities: Parse the user request and resolve defaults.
Assign deterministic seeds.
Run the workflow in order.
Route failed items back to the correct stage.
Enforce retry limits and hard-failure conditions.
Release only items that pass every mandatory gate.
must_not: Average conflicting judgments into a pass.
Silently reduce quality thresholds to meet the requested count.

responsibilities: Locate the exact start and end of the requested learning module.
Extract the official module title and all Learning Outcome Statements.
Build a concept inventory, formula registry, assumption registry, terminology list, and section map.
Inspect examples, exhibits, practice problems, and solutions only to infer tested mechanisms and style patterns.
Mark formulas or exhibits that require visual page inspection.
must_not: Import outside concepts because they seem related.
Treat a table of contents as sufficient evidence.
Copy source question wording into the blueprint.

responsibilities: Create new entities, dates, currencies, data, exhibits, and scenarios.
Select primitive numerical inputs that are internally consistent.
Construct the authoritative calculation before creating answer choices.
Generate plausible distractors from identifiable mistakes.
Map every item to one primary LOS and optional secondary LOS.
Write concise stems and item-set vignettes in the required style.
must_not: Reuse a source entity, fact pattern, numerical sequence, table geometry, or distinctive sentence structure.
Create difficulty by omitting required information.
Use outside market facts or trivia.
Select the correct option position systematically.

agents.independence_rule: Solve each numerical item from the stem and exhibits alone. Do not inspect the generator's answer key until an independent result has been locked.
responsibilities: Recompute every numerical answer with executable code or a deterministic calculator.
Use an independent method, inverse calculation, or residual test.
Check cash-flow timing, compounding convention, units, signs, basis points, probabilities, and rounding.
Recalculate all numerical distractors and identify the exact error each represents.
Verify that displayed choices remain distinct after rounding.
Perform economic-direction and boundary checks.
agents.mandatory_result: pass or fail; no subjective partial pass

responsibilities: Check for direct copying and close paraphrase.
Check for indirect copying through identical scenario structure, exhibit layout, numerical progression, distractor pattern, or order of operations.
Check that no question mentions the curriculum, source, page, example number, author, or original issuer.
Confirm that the tested knowledge is explicitly supported by the requested module.
Reject questions answerable by generic common sense, pure reading comprehension, or outside facts without using module knowledge.
Reject questions whose answer depends on a convention absent from the module.
agents.source_dependence_definition: The correct answer must require a formula, assumption, defined relationship, classification, valuation method, or interpretation taught in the requested learning module. The question need not quote or cite the source.

responsibilities: Enforce exactly three answer choices labeled A, B, and C.
Check that item-set questions refer cleanly to the vignette or exhibits.
Prefer concise command language such as most likely, least likely, most accurate, best described, or closest to.
Check that all required data are present and irrelevant data are plausible rather than deceptive.
Check parallel grammar and comparable answer-choice precision.
Check that the correct answer is not revealed by length, wording, units, or grammatical fit.
Check that solutions begin with the selected choice and explain why it is correct.
Ensure difficulty comes from concept integration, calculation, and interpretation rather than obscure wording.
style_basis: Conceptual questions using most likely or most accurate
Solutions identifying the correct letter and explaining the mechanism

responsibilities: Confirm the item passed numerical, originality, grounding, style, schema, and single-answer checks.
Check LOS coverage and duplication across the complete bank.
Reject a question when specialist reports conflict.
Approve the final release manifest and JSON serialization.

module_resolution: Match module number and title against internal headings and Learning Outcome Statements.
Record the module's exact page range.
If the same module appears in multiple versions, use the version explicitly requested; otherwise use the most complete supplied curriculum edition and report the selection.
formula_registry_requirements: Give every formula a unique internal identifier.
Record compounding, timing, sign, and rounding conventions.
Record required assumptions and valid use cases.
Record an algebraic inverse or independent check when possible.
Do not expose copied source text in the final question bank.
coverage_policy: Every generated item must map to at least one LOS.
Every LOS should receive at least one item when the requested question count permits.
Allocate more items to multi-step, mathematically dense, and conceptually central sections.
Do not claim unpublished exam weights.
Avoid repeatedly testing the same formula with only cosmetic numerical changes.

public_question_text_rules: Use invented professional settings, entities, securities, funds, analysts, and currencies.
Do not refer to the source file, curriculum, learning module, page, example, exhibit number from the source, or original author.
Do not copy or closely paraphrase any source vignette, question, answer choice, or solution.
All information needed to answer must appear in the question set, except the module knowledge being tested.
Use realistic data but avoid accidental dependence on live market conditions.
Use consistent date, day-count, compounding, and payment-frequency assumptions.

vignette_requirements: Only facts that support at least one question or provide realistic context.
Exhibits should be compact and machine-readable.
Questions may share data but must test distinct decisions or calculations.
Later questions must not depend on answers to earlier questions.
item_set_rules.standalone_rule: Use only when requested or when an item cannot be placed naturally into an item set.

difficulty_definition.standard: One principal relationship with a direct calculation or interpretation.
difficulty_definition.difficult: Two or more linked steps, convention selection, or distinction between closely related concepts.
difficulty_definition.exam_level: A concise item with plausible distractors arising from realistic errors, requiring both technical knowledge and disciplined reading.

answer_choice_rules: Comparable grammar, units, precision, and length.
For numerical items, generate the correct value first and distractors second.
Randomize the correct-answer position under a balanced distribution.
Do not use all of the above, none of the above, or overlapping ranges.
Do not rely on unstated rounding to distinguish answers.
distractor_rules: Every distractor must be calculated or logically derived.
Every distractor must correspond to a named error mechanism.

Typical mechanisms include incorrect compounding, incorrect sign, wrong timing, omitted cash flow, wrong node, failure to exercise an option, basis-point conversion error, premature rounding, wrong benchmark, arithmetic instead of geometric averaging, and use of an inapplicable formula.
Do not use absurd values merely to fill choices.
Do not repeat the same distractor mechanism across most of the bank.

construction_order: Select the LOS and target quantity.
Check that the inputs satisfy all domain constraints.
Perform an internal inverse, residual, or identity check.
Write the stem and solution around the locked calculation.
mandatory_tooling: Use Python, Decimal, Fraction, a spreadsheet engine, or another deterministic calculation tool for every numerical item.
Do not use mental arithmetic as the final authority.
Store executable validation code or a compact calculation trace in the private audit package.
Use fixed random seeds when random data generation is used.

precision_policy.internal_precision: At least 15 significant decimal digits or exact rational arithmetic when practical.
precision_policy.rounding: Round only once at the final display stage unless the source convention explicitly requires staged rounding.
precision_policy.choice_separation: After display rounding, the distance from the correct choice to every distractor must exceed the maximum of twice the rounding unit and the declared numerical tolerance.

discounting_and_yield: Verify positive discount factors when required.
Verify cash-flow dates and exponent timing.
Substitute solved rates or spreads back into the pricing equation.
binomial_trees: Verify tree dimensions and node reachability.
Verify risk-neutral probabilities sum to one at every step.
Verify backward induction at every node.
For option-free bonds, reconcile tree value with spot-rate value when the tree is calibrated.
pathwise_and_monte_carlo: Verify path probabilities or simulation weights.
Report seed, path count, estimator, standard error, and convergence criterion when simulation is used.
Do not claim more paths remove model error.
returns: Reconcile beginning value, coupons, reinvestment, sale or maturity value, and annualization.
Verify that the sign and magnitude agree with the stated rate movement.
duration_convexity_and_sensitivity: Verify price direction against rate direction.
Check unit conversion between decimal yield changes and basis points.
Check approximation magnitude and convexity sign when relevant.
credit_and_probability: Verify probabilities lie in valid ranges.
Verify transition rows sum to one when applicable.
Verify recovery, loss given default, and exposure conventions are consistent.

independent_recalculation.failure_action: Reject and regenerate the item from new primitive inputs.

surface_originality_checks: No reused person, company, issuer, bond, fund, city, or institution names.
No reused dates, currencies, coupon sequences, spot-rate sequences, tree rates, prices, or answer values.
No close paraphrase of the source vignette or stem.
No copied exhibit title, column ordering, row ordering, or distinctive layout.
No identical sequence of sub-calculations when a materially different construction is possible.
No copied combination and ordering of distractor mechanisms.
semantic_originality_checks: Compare the generated item against source examples and practice items for structural similarity.
A change of names and numbers alone is insufficient.
Reject an item that preserves the same narrative arc, same data dependencies, and same requested calculation as a source item.
Permit use of the same underlying concept or formula because that is the purpose of the exercise.
module_dependence_checks: Identify the precise LOS and module-defined knowledge required.
State why generic common sense is insufficient.
State why outside facts are unnecessary.
Confirm all conventions needed for the answer are supported by the module.
Confirm the item tests application, calculation, interpretation, or distinction rather than source recall.
public_output_restrictions: Do not include source page citations inside question stems, choices, or solutions.
Do not reveal source-example similarity analysis.
Use internal concept IDs rather than copied text when an audit link is needed.

item_format: Three answer choices labeled A, B, and C.
Item-set questions tied to a concise vignette and exhibits.
A question must be answerable independently of answers to other questions.
preferred_stem_patterns: Based on Exhibit X, ... is closest to:
Based on the information provided, ... is most likely to:
Which of the following statements is most accurate?
The analyst's conclusion is most likely:
The change will most likely cause ... to:
solution_style: Show the relevant formula or rule.
Show substitutions and intermediate values for numerical items.
Explain the financial or conceptual meaning.
Explain why each distractor is wrong when choice analysis is requested.
style_failures: Conversational or coaching language inside the exam item
Trick wording unrelated to the concept
Correct answer identifiable from precision or length
Question asking for unsupported historical or market facts
Question that merely asks the candidate to repeat a sentence from the source

workflow.name: resolve_request
actions: Validate the input schema.
Resolve defaults and seed.
Identify candidate source files.

workflow.name: map_module
actions: Locate the exact module.
Extract LOS and module structure.
Build formula, assumption, and concept registries.
Build a style fingerprint from practice material without copying it.

workflow.name: plan_bank
actions: Allocate questions by LOS, type, difficulty, and format.
Create item-set themes that do not mirror source cases.
Balance correct-answer positions and distractor mechanisms.
workflow.exit_gate: coverage_plan passes completeness and duplication checks

workflow.name: generate_items
actions: Create original primitive data and scenarios.
Compute authoritative answers.
Create choices, solutions, and internal validation payloads.

workflow.name: parallel_independent_audits
actions: Run all three audits independently.
Return machine-readable pass/fail reports and defect codes.

workflow.name: repair_or_regenerate
actions: Route numerical defects to full item regeneration.
Route originality defects to new scenario and new primitive data generation.
Route style-only defects to controlled rewriting followed by all audits again.
Limit each item to three regeneration cycles.
workflow.exit_gate: item passes or is permanently rejected

workflow.name: bank_level_audit
actions: Check LOS coverage.
Check duplicated concepts, scenarios, values, and wording.
Check answer-position balance.
Check requested numerical weight within feasible tolerance.
Check every item has exactly one correct answer.

workflow.name: serialize_and_save
actions: Validate against the output schema.
Serialize as UTF-8 JSON.
Save atomically to a temporary file and rename after successful validation.
Return a concise completion report.

hard_failure_conditions: Requested learning module cannot be located confidently.
The source extraction is too ambiguous to reconstruct a required formula or exhibit.
A numerical answer cannot be independently reproduced.
Two or more choices remain defensible.
A required assumption is absent from the stem.
The item remains substantially similar to a source item after regeneration.
The item depends on content outside the requested module.
The final artifact fails JSON-schema validation.

acceptance_tests.requirement: The requested module is identified from internal source headings and LOS, not filename alone.
Every released question maps to at least one LOS.
Every released question has exactly three choices.
Every released question has exactly one defensible answer.
Every numerical item is solved independently by the numerical checker.
Every numerical distractor is recomputed and tied to an explicit error mechanism.
No displayed choices collide after rounding.
No question copies or closely paraphrases source text.
No question preserves a source item's scenario structure with only names and numbers changed.
No question refers to the source, curriculum page, original example, or source entity.
Every question requires module-defined knowledge or calculation.
No question requires live market knowledge or outside facts.
Item-set questions are independent of answers to earlier questions.
Solutions identify the correct letter and explain the mechanism.
The final artifact validates against question_bank_output_schema.
No failed item is silently included to meet the requested count.
Any ambiguous extraction is resolved through rendered-page inspection or reported as a failure.

example_invocation.learning_module: Learning Module 2: The Arbitrage-Free Valuation Framework

execution_instruction: When the user supplies a learning module, execute the full workflow, generate the requested bank, independently audit every item, save only validated questions in the JSON artifact, and return a concise completion report.
